transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, I really don't want to sound difficult or unreasonable. But for almost two years now—ever since a big commission I had—I've just been unable to shake this certainty I have about my ensemble. It feels like a few people in the group started, well, quietly undermining my work as the director. 

It’s just little things, you know? Like sudden schedule changes, or odd seating choices, or just... little comments they make during rehearsals. And, I mean, they’re always very polite about it and they'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain why a change happened, and I always try to be agreeable and understanding, but... I just can't shake the certainty that it's intentional. 

Does that make sense? I hope it’s okay that I came in to talk to you about this, I just haven't been sure how to handle it.
Have you ever spoken to someone you trust—like a close friend or family member—about these suspicions, and if so, what was their reaction to what you were telling them?

Um, well... I haven't really talked to anyone about it, to be honest. I mean, I hope that's alright, I just... I didn't want to worry my family or, you know, make things awkward with my friends. They all know the people in the ensemble, and I'd hate to create any kind of drama or make anyone uncomfortable. 

I guess I just thought it was better to keep it to myself, you know? I really try to be easy to work with, and I didn't want anyone to think I was being overly sensitive or complaining too much. Is that... is it normal to kind of keep things like this quiet? I just really want to handle it the right way without upsetting anyone.
Do you find yourself feeling this same way about people in other areas of your life, such as with neighbors, acquaintances, or people you encounter in public?

Oh, um, no. No, definitely not. I hope I didn't give the impression that I'm, you know, suspicious of everyone... because I'm really not. I actually get along very well with my neighbors, and just people I meet day to day. 

It's really just... just this specific situation with the ensemble. I try very hard to be friendly and open with everyone else, and I don't want you to think I'm someone who just assumes the worst of people or looks for trouble. I really value being on good terms with everyone. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's a good sign that it's only happening with the group, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual sensations, like hearing voices or sounds that others around you did not seem to notice?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely nothing like that. Um... I haven't heard any voices or, you know, sounds that aren't there. 

I hope I didn't say anything that made it seem like my mind was playing tricks on me? I promise I'm completely clear-headed. It's really just... just the actual things I see happening with the ensemble. I would absolutely tell you if there was anything else, I really would. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need. 

It's a good thing that I don't have anything like that going on, isn't it? I just really want to assure you that I'm completely fine in that regard.
When you say you are certain these colleagues are intentionally undermining your work, what do you believe is their ultimate goal or reason for doing so?

Um, well... I mean, I don't think they're trying to ruin my life or anything terrible like that. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm accusing them of being evil or, you know, malicious people. They're very talented musicians. 

I just... I think maybe they just don't want me directing this particular piece? Like, maybe they feel they know better how it should be interpreted, and they just want me to step down or hand it over to someone else. Which, I mean, I guess I can understand if they're passionate about the music, right? I just wish they'd talk to me about it instead of... well, doing the things they're doing. 

I'm not trying to make them look like villains, I promise. I really just want to figure out how to smooth things over so we can all just focus on the music. Is that... does that sound like a reasonable explanation to you? I really don't want to come across as someone who thinks everyone is out to get them.
Could you tell me a little bit more about how you prepare for these rehearsals, perhaps starting from when you first wake up on the day of a performance?

Um, sure, I can tell you about that. I hope it doesn't sound too, you know, boring or routine. But on a rehearsal day, I just wake up and try to keep things as normal as possible. 

Outside of this whole issue with the ensemble, I'm really trying to keep everything else on track. I still get up and run most mornings—I think staying active is a good way to keep a clear head, don't you? And I'm still meeting all my deadlines and keeping up with my composing work. I don't let this situation stop me from doing my job, I promise. 

And things at home with my wife are... they're basically steady. We have a good routine. I try really hard not to let any stress from the rehearsals spill over into my home life, because I know how important it is to keep a good balance. 

So, my preparation is really just about staying focused and professional. Does that sound like a healthy way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm managing everything okay despite the... the tension with the group.
Do you believe that these colleagues have ever directly confronted you or formally complained to the ensemble's board or management about your direction?

Um, no... no, they haven't done anything official like that. Nobody has said anything to my face, and... and as far as I know, there haven't been any complaints to the board or to management at all. 

I've been trying really, really hard to make sure it doesn't escalate to that level, you know? I feel like if management had to get involved, it would just reflect poorly on everyone, and I really want to be seen as someone who can handle his ensemble. So I just try to keep my head down and do my job on the podium as best as I can. 

I think it's a good sign that they haven't filed any formal complaints, don't you? It makes me hopeful that maybe this is just a... a temporary thing, and we can work it out eventually without making a big scene. I'm doing the right thing by just trying to keep it professional and not reacting, aren't I?
Do you feel that these specific colleagues are working together in a coordinated, secret group to undermine you, or do you feel that each of them is acting on their own individual initiative?

Um, well, I don't think it's some kind of, you know, secret conspiracy or a coordinated plot or anything dramatic like that. I really hope I haven't made it sound like I think they're having secret meetings about me in dark rooms. That would sound pretty crazy, wouldn't it? 

I think it's more just... maybe they individually feel the same way about the piece, and they're just sort of feeding off each other's energy in rehearsal? Like, one person starts dragging the tempo, and the other just kind of goes along with it because they're used to playing together. 

It feels more like they just happen to agree with each other rather than them teaming up against me on purpose. Does that make sense? I really try to give them the benefit of the doubt. I don't want to be the kind of director who assumes the worst about his musicians. I think it's better to just view it as individual artistic differences, right?
Do you feel that your approach to this specific piece of music is uniquely important or that your vision for it is something that perhaps only you are capable of fully realizing?

Um, no, I don't think it's anything like that. I really don't want to come across as arrogant or, you know, like I have some kind of huge ego about my work. I think that would be a terrible trait for a director to have, don't you?

I mean, I care about the piece, of course I do. I put a lot of work into it, and I have a specific interpretation in mind. But I certainly don't think I'm the only person in the world who could understand it or perform it. That would be a really unhealthy way to look at music, right? It's supposed to be collaborative. 

I just... I just want us to play it well, together. I'm really just trying to do a good job and be a competent director. I'm not trying to be some kind of misunderstood genius or anything. I hope I haven't given you the impression that I think too highly of myself? I really value being grounded and practical about my work.

When you are in public settings, such as at a coffee shop or a grocery store, do you ever feel as though strangers are paying special attention to you or that their conversations or actions are somehow related to you?

Um, no, definitely not. I don't feel like strangers are watching me or talking about me at all. I mean, I'm just a normal guy getting coffee or picking up groceries, you know? There's nothing special about me that would make people stop and stare.

I'd feel pretty self-centered if I walked around thinking everyone was paying attention to me. That sounds like something someone who's really out of touch with reality would think, doesn't it? I just mind my own business when I'm out and about. 

I really try to just blend in and be polite to people. I hope that's normal? I mean, most people just go about their day without worrying about what strangers are doing, right? That's exactly how I am. I promise I don't have any weird thoughts like that.
